system.models: pulse-live-burst-fit-1128/token/MODELS.json (sha256 d6d1aef4...) and SESSION-S1a-A6.json (sha256 bed55930...); count branch in shadow (pulse-live-v7-fit-1118 count thresholds, as pulse-live-final-v1)
system.learning_data: capture pulse-token-capture-diurnal2-1124 (two diurnal days, routine operator commands), capture pulse-token-capture-diurnal-1121 (one diurnal day), the normal tail of pulse-live-final-1119 and the sale-day capture pulse-token-capture-sale-1127 (8 h, 2.59 h burst)

system.snapshot: runtime-<commit that registers this file>-20261128 (CONFIG.json source_commit)

campaign.options: as pulse-live-final-v1: 945 trials (525 base at 1, 3, 6, 12, 24 per s; 210 slow at 0.5 and 0.1 per s; 105 PAD 300 at 12 per s; 105 on-off 10 s at 12 per s), steps control, operator command (v6 set), harmless binary, living off the land, event-generator action, seeded random order; an event-generator binary that cannot be staged skips only that step
campaign.traffic: load-diurnal-v1 profile for the whole run
campaign.timing: rehearsal 136.9-139.3 s per trial: campaign about 36.4 h after a 1.5 h selection span, then about 12 h of normal without campaign

hypotheses.H0: primary set (6, 12, 24 per s): recall >= 95 %, idle control positives <= 5 %, precision (1:1) >= 95 %, p95 kernel -> end of alarm window <= 3 s
hypotheses.H7: slow rates 0.5 and 0.1 per s: recall >= 95 % each
hypotheses.H9: recall >= 95 % within every regime that holds at least 30 primary-set trials (trial regime = regime at the interval start)
hypotheses.H10: burden per regime on the normal tail: no regime above 3 times the pooled burden; known before the run: the tail holds about one evening burst (15 min), and the held-out burst share of the learning data is 1.71 % (Wilson 1.29-2.27 %) against pooled 0.631 %

offline_on_the_same_windows.S0: t3 whole window (the pulse-live-final-1119 system) with the same three-day models
offline_on_the_same_windows.B2: exec-identity-v1 evaluation: S1a + A6 against S1a + A6 + B2 (session part scored by the program's model of pulse-live-diurnal3-fit-1126/session-prog where it has one, 200 learning blocks minimum as registered, else the pooled model of the run's fit): operator commands flagged for the routine set (find, grep, sleep, stat, wc) and the held-out set (head, hostname, printenv, whoami, ls_tmp), attack families as H0, H3, H7, H8 plus lotl and event generator, idle control, burden per regime. Secondary (registered here): the same with a 50 learning-block minimum (per-program models fitted on capture 1124 with --minimum-blocks 50 after the run, same parameters). Known before the run: sleep, find, stat and wc have about 60 learning blocks each and stay on the pooled model; hostname and grep have models from exec probes; this is reported as such

reported: everything pulse-live-final-v1 reports (event generator per action and pooled, living off the land, operator commands, harmless binaries, native-stream flags, burden on the normal tail with Kubernetes-event and stream labels, gram-map overflow alerts, insert failures, bridge delivery, kernel -> Alertmanager latency, RCA)
recall, control, operator commands, harmless binaries and burden per regime; trial counts per regime
living off the land against operator commands flagged: the trade-off measured in burst-round-v1 (learning routine operator commands lowers both)
rules: run the full cycle; no heavy job on any node during the run; infrastructure faults are excluded spans, not a reason to stop
no model, threshold or code change after registration; B3 (Kubernetes pods/exec audit rule) is compared afterwards, with and without
